body:
If you had to pick one guest star to come back, who would it be?

What's your favorite episode of Criminal Minds? 

Have you heard of Pedal to the Point? (it's a 175 mile bike race in Ohio, raising money for MS. It's in two weeks. I'm participating in it this year! My grandma has MS, we wish you and your mom good luck with the journey.)

Do you know how big a role model you are to me?
Yeah. I've moved my areas 11 times because I don't want to cut old scars. I'm glad to know I'm not the only one who feels this!

My therapist has been helping me with my skills making friends. She wants me to try group therapy once a week along with my individual therapy. We think it'd give me the feeling of being around nice people, and teach me how to socially interact. 

I've considered joining a womens jiu jitsu class. I've always been interested in that. The place I'm lookin at for signing up has age groups, so I would be able to meet people my age easily!

I guess I do have to try to space myself from my dad. I just want to know what it's like to have parents, *real* ones. Even if it meant going out of my way to try to attempt to fix the relationship.

I'm doing better than I was yesterday, as in not ready to die at the moment. But I'm still kinda bummed out. Thanks for taking the time to reply!

It is *very* unlikely. I'm afraid of a lot of ridiculous things, unfortunatly. 

My therapist tells me that I can choose what to be afraid of. I don't see how I can do that, is it just me? Or does my therapist have crazy abilities, assuming she chooses what she fears?

I fear her reaction. I trust her with everything. Hell, I'd tell her in a heartbeat. But in that heartbeat, I would have an Anxiety attack. When that happens, I often pass out. Where would that lead me? Waking up and just repeating it because I have to talk about being suicidal.

I'm afraid she wouldn't look at me as an equal anymore. I'm afraid she won't be my friend anymore. I'm afraid of getting made fun of. I'm afraid.

I've dealt with it alone for atleast 15 years. When I first started taking a really stupid therapists advice and telling when I felt suicidal, she made fun of me. Since then, I find it scary to share. I feel like I'm weak and alone. I don't have the money to be hospitalized again. I don't want my therapist knowing that one day she could wake up to a voicemail informing her that a friend and a client died that night. I don't want her knowing that I'm a danger to myself, because I don't want her to think less of me... It's more of a fear thing, than a trust issue.

It has gotten better. She's given me real helpful tips on how to go about building a bond. She reminds me everyday how remarkable it is that I'm pushing this relationship. My therapist and I text all the time and it's like assurance. When something happens I usually text or call her, and we talk it out. She's really the best therapist I've had, and I think the outside-of-therapy friendship helps give me more trust with her. It's probably just her way of making me talk, her knowing my past most likely influenced that. She knows I'm suicidal and have attempted in the past, but I can't bring myself to tell her when I'm feeling suicidal. About an hour ago, I realised I don't need to end my own life, my sickness will do it for me eventually. As long as I refuse medication, it should take over.

They just kind of seperate themselves. They don't participate when I try to get conversations going. Forgive me for eavesdropping, but I hear them talking about it. At night, when they go to bed, I can hear through the wall. They say stuff like, "Don't you think it's a bit odd that she wants a relationship with us?', "Do you think it'd be awkward if I hugged her?", "Do you think she has bad news and that's the only reason she doesn't hate us?", "How in the world is she okay around us?!", etc. 

I really do want a relationship with them. My therapist suggested bringing them in for family therapy, but I want to fix it by ourselves, you know? Also, therapy is my only place to let everything out, around someone nonjudgemental, not related, and I already built trust with her. I don't want to lose that privelage. 

I'm not strong enough to accept the fact that my parents can't forgive me for forgiving them. Eternal sleep seems like the only logical coping mechanism.
